stem: A Massachusetts-licensed health care facility has no on-site pharmacy. Its outside pharmacy provider wants to place an automated dispensing device (ADD) in a patient-care area. Before the ADD is used, what is the best compliance step?

choices.text: Use it once the pharmacy owns every medication loaded into the cabinet.
Obtain approval for the ADD's use and placement from the facility's licensing body.
Obtain only a new wholesaler permit for the outside pharmacy.
Begin use after the pharmacy's manager of record signs an internal memo.
Delay approval until the first Schedule II medication is stocked.

explanation.core_reasoning: A facility without an on-site pharmacy needs licensing-body approval for ADD use and placement.

choice_analysis.A: Ownership does not replace facility approval.
choice_analysis.C: A wholesaler permit is not the stated approval.
choice_analysis.E: Approval is not triggered only by C-II stock.

related_facts: The ADD policy applies to Massachusetts-licensed health care facilities.
explanation.mpje_trap: Confusing pharmacy ownership of stock with facility authorization.

reasoning_steps: Identify that the facility lacks an on-site pharmacy
